overview: This Senate resolution supports naming July 10, 2025, as Journeyman Lineworkers Recognition Day. Journeyman lineworkers are skilled workers who build and repair power lines, often in storms, disasters and harsh weather, to keep electricity flowing. The date marks the anniversary of the death of Henry Miller, the first president of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers union, who was killed in 1896 while restoring power in Washington, D.C. The resolution honors the sacrifices of lineworkers and encourages Americans to observe the day. The Senate agreed to it on July 10, 2025.
for: Supporters say it recognizes workers who take real risks, often during disasters, to keep homes, hospitals and businesses powered.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law, safety rule or spending.
